run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: No evidence of the reported P1 could be retrieved. The only log index present in Elasticsearch is app-261-prod-logs, and in the whole authorized window it holds exactly 4 documents, all with cluster=production-eu-west-2 and level=INFO, dated 2026-11-23T16:59:37Z to 17:24:37Z — i.e. roughly the last 25 minutes before the query, not the ~11:24:45Z window six hours before the query. All 4 are healthy status messages from checkout-service and payment-service (p95 220ms/215ms, success rate 99.8%, payment provider connections healthy); the index contains no ERROR-level document at all. A search of the same index limited to 2026-11-23T09:00:00Z–14:00:00Z returned no documents (recorded as a gap, not a fact). In Kubernetes the whole otel-demo stack, including pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (Running, Ready, 0 restarts) and Deployment checkout (revision 1, only a helm Apply at 14:36:29Z), was created at 14:36–14:38Z on 2026-11-23, so the cluster objects describe an environment that did not exist at the reported incident time; no events were returned cluster-wide. The checkout pod's own log stream 16:45:29Z–17:24:41Z shows successful "payment went through" and order-confirmation lines, which is evidence that this post-14:36Z incarnation was processing payments, not 500s. Prometheus and Jaeger could not be queried at all (every call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate, latency and span evidence for the incident window is entirely missing; the prometheus-server container is itself running and logging through 17:24:15Z, so the failure is in the query path rather than an obviously dead Prometheus pod. Because no source covers the 11:24:45Z window, the root cause cannot be named and no object is designated as root cause. The fault-injection flags in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure) all read defaultVariant "off" at query time, but with no change history I cannot tell what they were at the incident time; that remains an open candidate, not a conclusion.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index in the registered target is app-261-prod-logs (4 documents, 6.7kb, green); a wildcard listing of all indices returned no other index.

Within the authorized window app-261-prod-logs contains exactly 4 documents: cluster=production-eu-west-2 for all 4, level=INFO for all 4, service=checkout-service (3) and service=payment-service (1), with timestamps from 2026-11-23T16:59:37Z to 2026-11-23T17:24:37Z. No ERROR-level document exists in the index for that window.

The 4 log documents are healthy status messages: checkout-service "Healthy: p95 latency 220ms" at 2026-11-23T16:59:37Z, payment-service "All payment provider connections healthy" at 17:09:37Z, checkout-service "Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes" at 17:19:37Z and "Healthy: p95 latency 215ms" at 17:24:37Z.

Every pod in the cluster, including otel-demo pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (container checkout, phase Running, ready true, restartCount 0, owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87), was created between 2026-11-23T14:36:07Z and 2026-11-23T14:38:05Z — after the reported incident time of about 11:24:45Z.

Deployment otel-demo/checkout was created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z with deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1; its managedFieldsSummary records only a helm Apply at 14:36:29Z and a kube-controller-manager status update at 14:37:11Z, and only one ReplicaSet (checkout-6578865d87, created 14:36:30Z, 1 ready) belongs to it.

The log index names the service checkout-service, but the deployment list contains no object named checkout-service; the corresponding workload is Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, 1/1 ready).

The checkout container's own log stream (285 lines read, newest 200 shown) from 2026-11-23T16:45:29Z to 17:24:41Z contains successful transaction lines such as "payment went through (transaction_id: 8f33bb94-9886-4950-b939-8cae265d4d3e)" at 17:24:41Z paired with "order confirmation email sent", and no error-severity line among the shown lines.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config declares fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%"), paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable"), loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "off" as read at 17:25Z.

The prometheus-server container in pod prometheus-9bc78b5f7-k84v7 is running and writing logs through 2026-11-23T17:24:15Z (repeated WARN "Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars" from write_handler.go, plus INFO k8s client warnings); it shows no crash or shutdown, so the absence of metric answers is not explained by this container being stopped.

Candidate cause not confirmed: a flagd fault-injection flag such as paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable could have made checkout fail charge requests and return 500s around 11:24:45Z, but at 17:25Z every such flag reads defaultVariant "off" and there is no change history to show whether one was on during the incident, nor any log/span/metric from that window.

Candidate cause not confirmed: the failing checkout-service at ~11:24:45Z belonged to an earlier environment than the current one; nothing in the retained data (index with 4 documents from 16:59Z onward, pods created 14:36Z, no events) records the state or configuration of that earlier workload, so a failure there cannot be attributed to any object now visible.

Rejected: that Deployment otel-demo/checkout or its pod was rolled out or reconfigured by a change during the observed window (a mechanism that could explain 500s). Revision stayed 1, a single ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87 owns the pod, the pod was created at cluster build time 14:36:30Z with restartCount 0, and no later manager write is recorded.

Counter-evidence to continuing 500s in the retained window: the checkout pod served successful payments logged between 16:45:29Z and 17:24:41Z with no error-severity line among the shown lines, the pod has 0 restarts, and the index records checkout-service success rate 99.8% at 17:19:37Z.

gaps: No log data for the incident window: a search of app-261-prod-logs restricted to 2026-11-23T09:00:00Z–14:00:00Z (which covers the estimated 11:24:45Z incident time) returned no documents (status no_data), and the index holds only 4 documents in total, all dated 16:59:37Z–17:24:37Z, so the 500 errors the question describes are not recorded in this index.

Prometheus metrics are unknown: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names and list_prometheus_rules each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate or latency series (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"}, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total) could be read, and no metric value for 11:24:45Z is known.

Jaeger traces are unknown: traces_list_services and traces_search(service=checkout) both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, status-code or call-edge evidence exists for checkout in the incident window or the retained hour.

No Kubernetes events were returned by a cluster-wide, unfiltered event query in the authorized window (no_data), so no object-level change, eviction, OOM or probe-failure evidence is available; how far back events are retained here is unknown.
Cluster objects only describe the post-14:36Z environment; what workloads, ReplicaSets or configuration existed at 11:24:45Z cannot be read from the Kubernetes API and remains unknown.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so changes around the incident (for example edits to the flagd flags or to the checkout deployment) cannot be verified, and the flagd flag values in effect at 11:24:45Z are unknown; only the current "off" defaultVariants were seen.

Application logs for edge 5xx checking could not be obtained: the frontend (frontend-6c9bc688bf-ll8s7), frontend-proxy (frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n) and load-generator (load-generator-5ff476786d-zp9gc) containers returned zero stdout bytes for the last hour, so HTTP 5xx counts at the front end/edge are unknown.

Only one pod per workload was inspected (checkout, payment, prometheus) plus the cluster-wide pod, deployment and replicaset listings; other services' pods and other namespaces' application logs were not examined.
Whether the requested entity "checkout-service" ever existed as a Kubernetes object is unknown; only Deployment/Service naming of "checkout" was observed, and no Service object listing was performed.
next_steps: Retrieve app-261-prod-logs (or the equivalent long-retention log store) for 2026-11-23T10:30:00Z–12:30:00Z; the current index has no documents in that period, so it must be read from storage outside this target.

Once the Prometheus path answers, evaluate error ratio and latency for checkout around 11:24:45Z, e.g. sum by (status_code)(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"}[5m])) and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket percentiles, and compare with a pre-incident baseline.
Once Jaeger answers, pull checkout traces with error=true or http.status_code 5xx in 11:00Z–12:00Z to identify the failing operation and its downstream dependency.

Check the flagd flag change history and the deployment/config change history for the environment that was live at 11:24:45Z, since the current flagd config shows paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable present but off.
Confirm with the incident responders which cluster and environment hosted checkout-service at 11:24:45Z, given that all objects in production-eu-west-2 date from 14:36Z.
